steps.notes: Completed at 3b4732be. Missing-owner completions leave PageSlot state unchanged. Verified cargo test -p tx-subsystems --lib owned_request_, cargo test -p tx-subsystems --lib page_backed -- --test-threads=1 (148 passed), cargo -q xtask unit, legacy dual-map cleanup scan, and git diff --check.

steps.title: Migrate PageBacked submission, resume, completion, and fsync
steps.notes: Completed at a16958f2. Writeback leases and read targets are retained at admission by OwnedFileIoRequest; every initial/resume planning and queue failure reaches its one terminalizer. A completion requires a matching read/writeback payload, so a control-only owner is poison and cannot settle PageSlot. Legacy fsync submission rows were removed; FileFsyncState retains only the frontier and calls FsPageBacking::fsync_file after it completes. Verified cargo test -p tx-subsystems --lib page_backed -- --test-threads=1 (154 passed), Tier 1 admission tests, cargo -q xtask unit, static legacy cleanup scans, cargo xtask progress validate, cargo xtask lint docs, and git diff --check.

steps.title: Add MutationHandle and owned cross-yield tokens
steps.notes: Completed: private MutationHandle now owns prepared journal records, optional JournalExtentToken, data/commit request IDs, phase-local error state, and checkpoint retry state. JournalFsyncSource is a compatibility re-export but its callback orchestration moved to mutation_lifecycle.rs; a data failure consumes the handle and releases its ring extent exactly once. This bounded slice retains the existing immutable after-images inside PreparedJournalTransaction but does not yet add explicit frozen-read/allocator-claim tokens, AbortDraining, CommitUnknown/RecoveryOnly, or real FUA/flush durability. Verified cargo test -p tx-ext4 --test mutation_lifecycle, cargo test -p tx-ext4 --test journal_prepared_transaction, cargo test -p tx-ext4 --lib --no-default-features, cargo -q xtask unit, scoped rustfmt/diff checks. cargo xtask lint arch ran: the touched ext4 journal length finding was eliminated, but the repository still has 90 unrelated pre-existing architecture lint findings.

steps.title: Close abort drain, commit uncertainty, and checkpoint retry
steps.notes: Completed: MutationHandle now records AbortRequested -> AbortDraining -> RolledBack for known pre-commit data or commit failure, releasing its JournalExtentToken once the aggregate graph completion reports terminal failure. The explicit commit_unknown request-ID path retains the handle and ring extent, records the source error, and gates new writeback/fsync planning with RecoveryOnly/EIO. Checkpoint failure records a source error but retains CommittedNeedsSettlement and its extent for retry; a later successful checkpoint is still the sole release route. This source-local gate precedes Task 13 errseq/open-file cursor and mounted-instance publication; Task 7 still must prove real FUA/flush ordering. Verified lifecycle, prepared-transaction, ext4 library, workspace unit, scoped rustfmt, and diff checks.

steps.title: Implement real FUA and flush durability
steps.notes: Completed: BlockDeviceOps exposes immutable FUA/flush capabilities plus write options; BlockDeviceDispatchAdapter transfers BlockFlags::FUA to a capable device and rejects unsupported FUA rather than silently dropping it. RV64 virtio PCI/MMIO truthfully advertise flush=true and fua=false because the present virtio driver exposes flush but no FUA write API. JournalTransactionPlan therefore emits ordered explicit flush fences after the journal body and commit, plus after the clean checkpoint write, rather than attaching an unsupported FUA flag. Verified dispatch_adapter_passes_fua_to_capable_device, default_device_rejects_fua_instead_of_ignoring_it, journal_transaction_plan (3), mutation_lifecycle (4), cargo check -p tx-drivers, cargo -q xtask unit (639 tx-shims tests), scoped rustfmt, and git diff --check. This does not admit a production RW path, runtime device-capability selection, tail/cache settlement, replay, or QEMU durability evidence; Task 8 remains next.

steps.title: Gate replay on recovery state and refresh caches
steps.notes: Completed: recovery admission exposes Superblock::needs_recovery and recover_if_required; a clean ext4 superblock skips stale JBD2 replay, while recovery-required runs replay plus durable journal clean. JBD2 superblock CRC32C has valid and invalid witnesses; unsupported descriptor/commit checksum layouts fail closed. BlockImage::barrier is mandatory and the production bridge forwards it to the registered block device. RW admission persists recovery-required before a journalled mutation. A weak mount settlement observer invalidates pager image, extent mapping, lookup, directory, inode metadata, and bridge block caches after durable checkpoint; JournalExtentToken remains retained until that settlement returns, then tail reclaim releases it. Verified jbd2_recovery (9), pager_mock (17), tx-ext4 library (35), mutation_lifecycle (5), tx-fs bridge (6), scoped rustfmt, and git diff --check. This is not product recovery acceptance: Task 9 revoke/deferred-free, complete mutation vertical slices, mount settlement, production cutover, QEMU crash, e2fsck, and xfstests evidence remain pending.

steps.title: Add revoke records and deferred-free ownership
steps.notes: Completed: immutable Ext4MutationPlan values canonicalize paired RevokeRecord and DeferredFreeClaim entries; JBD2 reserves and stages an optional revoke page between metadata and commit, and its durable graph orders that page before commit. MutationHandle owns the deferred-free claims from admission through cache observer settlement and JournalExtentToken tail reclaim, so test-only reuse remains EBUSY until tail reclaim. Replay recognizes the optional revoke page, validates its sequence, includes it in cursor accounting, and suppresses matching same-transaction stale after-images. Verified jbd2_transaction_image (2), jbd2_recovery (10), journal_transaction_plan (4), mutation_lifecycle (6), cargo -q xtask unit (639 + 114 + 35 + 166), scoped rustfmt, and git diff --check. This is not a production free path: truncate/unlink/rename-overwrite/orphan cleanup remain fail-closed and require Task 11/12 vertical slices plus QEMU crash/replay, e2fsck, and xfstests evidence.

steps.title: Migrate setattr as the first complete vertical slice
steps.notes: Completed: mutation-journal mounts now bind the mount-owned JournalMutationRuntime back to Ext4FsInstance for metadata-only admission. FsOps::serialize_inode_meta admits exactly one supported SetAttr class (mode, owner, or times) through Ext4Pager::plan_setattr plus JournalMutationRuntime::begin_mutation, while size/nlink/blocks/flags and mixed-class updates remain fail-closed for Task 11/12. Ext4 overrides public chmod_inode and chown_inode to admit SetAttr::Mode and SetAttr::Owner directly; tests prove these public paths create an active journal transaction frontier without any direct home write. Verified cargo test -p tx-ext4 --lib --no-default-features -- --test-threads=1 (39), cargo test -p tx-ext4 --test mutation_lifecycle -- --test-threads=1 (7), cargo -q xtask unit (646 + 114 + 39 + 166), and scoped rustfmt.

steps.title: Migrate buffered data, bounded extents, and truncate
steps.notes: Completed: bounded Tier 1 data/truncate is converged. PageBacked can retain a multi-page PageDataLease, group a captured FileFsyncFrontier into contiguous same-generation batches, and submit one OwnedFileIoRequest for a multi-page writeback range. Ext4 validates Direct multi-page sources without copying payload bytes, plans already-mapped writeback through JournalMutationRuntime, and keeps allocation or unsupported extent growth fail-closed before dirty publication. Truncate admits metadata-only size changes plus the bounded inline extent-leaf tail-free shape with inode/bitmap/group/superblock after-images, revoke records, and deferred-free claims; broader extent-depth growth remains Tier 2/out-of-scope under the capability ledger. The remaining reservation cleanup gap is closed in this slice: successful truncate now clears buffered-write reservations for pages at or beyond the new EOF, with regression coverage for truncate-before-flush. Verified cargo test -p tx-ext4 --lib --no-default-features truncate_before_flush -- --test-threads=1, previous Task 11 host suites, the fresh 1000-cut Task 16 receipt, and receipt-only verification.

Open-unlink deferral and closed zero-link destroy are covered by runtime tests and the Tier 1 role scenario; singleton classic-orphan cleanup was fixed before the final live run. The former crash-time orphan/recovery, crash-truncate replay, pinned xfstests, and immutable receipt blockers are closed by fresh run task16-live-retry-20260804: G0-G7 passed, D0-D12 crash cuts completed 1000/1000, TEST/SCRATCH/WORKLOAD e2fsck were clean, Docker-backed pinned xfstests passed 8/8, and historical D5 crash-cut-0213 plus D10 crash-cut-0725 did not recur. Directory split/rebalance, orphan_file, and arbitrary deeper shapes remain Tier 2/out-of-scope, not Task 12 blockers.

risks: A direct pager call can create a second durability domain unless G0 rejects every production callsite.
A committed transaction with checkpoint failure requires retained authority and retry; treating it as rollback corrupts the live view.
FUA metadata without device capability enforcement can make fsync appear durable while the medium is not ordered.
Lazy detach can withdraw topology while DMA or settlement remains live; the MountPayload pin must outlive topology removal.
Host contract tests and reused serial logs can be mistaken for product evidence without fresh QEMU, immutable image, e2fsck, and xfstests receipts.
